theme: Student food insecurity in the United States

cards.label: Scale
cards.claim: An estimated 23 percent of college students experienced food insecurity in 2020.

cards.label: Severity
cards.claim: Among food-insecure students, 2.2 million reported multiple instances of eating less than they should or skipping meals because they could not afford enough food.

cards.label: Policy gap
cards.claim: Of food-insecure students who were potentially eligible for SNAP, 59 percent did not report receiving benefits.

sources.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Estimated Eligibility and Receipt among Food Insecure College Students

limitations: The student estimates are based on 2020 NPSAS data, not a live 2026 count.
Food insecurity is a measured economic and social condition; it is not the same measure as hunger.
The 59 percent figure applies only to food-insecure students who were potentially eligible for SNAP.
